basis: Ataxia, abasia and generalized hypotonia define a neurologic motor syndrome; no evidence of primary muscle disease.
Inherited bile transport/metabolic disorder causing recurrent intrahepatic cholestasis; hearing impairment and pancreatitis occur in only 5-29%.
Barium deposition defines a pulmonary pneumoconiosis, even though deposits generally do not impair lung function.
Oxidative phosphorylation disorder with cardiomyopathy 9/9 and anemia 7/7; liver dysfunction 5/9. Hearing loss reported in 1/1 omitted under cap and limited sampling.
Fibrosing inflammation of skeletal muscle; inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune or immune-mediated mechanism.
Inherited skin fragility with acral blistering and erosions; dental abnormalities occur in only 5-29%; PLEC alone does not establish muscle involvement.
Posterior parietal lesions cause visuospatial and gaze dysfunction; the definition explicitly excludes underlying ocular abnormalities.
Germ cell tumor arising in the vulva, a reproductive organ outside the axes; no additional organ involvement established.
Painful neuropathy is a disorder of peripheral nerves; no other organ disease is established.
Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism defines endocrine dysfunction; anosmia and Duane anomaly each reported in 1/3 patients, supporting neurologic and ocular involvement with small-sample uncertainty.
Tumor originates in odontogenic epithelium; roughly 95-99% are intraosseous, directly occupying and often destroying mandibular or maxillary bone.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no single organ is consistently affected across the group.
Inherited renal magnesium transport defect causes primary hypomagnesemia; intellectual disability is a defining feature.
Definition restricts this neoplasm to ovaries and fallopian tubes; reproductive organs have no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not established.
Lysosomal storage with hepatic dysfunction and splenic disease/hypersplenism; pulmonary dysfunction 5/8. Bone loss 30-79% omitted under cap; neuropathy only 5-29%.
Congenital hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; neurodevelopmental abnormalities reported in 30-79% support hypoglycemic neural injury. Transient autonomic symptoms add no organs.
Tumor arises in rectal mucosa; neuroendocrine differentiation alone adds no endocrine axis. Listed pulmonary carcinoid is a separate tumor, not rectal organ involvement.
Defined by pulmonary vascular occlusion with acute lung injury; underlying sickle cell disease is a separately diagnosed blood disorder.
Plasminogen deficiency causes destructive fibrinous mucosal lesions: ocular disease 80-99%, gingival disease 30-79%; hydrocephalus reported in 2/2, with small-cohort uncertainty.
Unilateral Madelung deformity is a structural growth deformity of the distal radius and wrist.
Obliterative disease of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts; malabsorption and prolonged prothrombin time reflect cholestasis rather than separate direct organ injury.
Uterine trophoblastic tumor has reproductive origin. Lung metastases are characteristic, but involvement of at least 30% across all cases is not established by the supplied evidence.
Testicular germ cell tumor; reproductive origin without established endocrine gland dysfunction or common direct damage to another axis.
Angiosarcoma is a malignant neoplasm of vascular endothelium, supporting the vessel axis; the prostatic reproductive site itself has no axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss in 4/4 patients; delayed speech follows hearing impairment and does not establish independent neurologic damage.
